The administration frequently receives inquiries from care homes, schools,
government facilities and other businesses to include an accessible ramp for the loading zone in
front of their facilities to accommodate people using mobility devices. The proposed policy amendments
in front of you would define that criteria and regulations for the installation of these accessible
loading zones to accommodate the needs of people using mobility aids. The administration has completed
a one year pilot project installing on-street accessibility ramps in a loading zone at three locations.
To review and confirm design standards and also gather feedback from the stakeholders.
Each partner organization funded the installation costs and committed to maintaining and monitoring
the infrastructure and also engaging with the city of Saskatoon throughout the pilot project.
Appendix one of the report includes some photographs of the three locations. To collect feedback
on the pilot project, direct communications with the targeted stakeholders took place via site visits,
meetings and emails. A survey was conducted in the spring of 2025 with pilot site organizations and
user groups. Overall the feedback demonstrated support for the preparation of an accessible
loading zone policy that provides guidance and regulations regarding the installation of infrastructure
to provide an accessible loading zone. The proposed policy amendment will accomplish the following.
Establish a request process for the installation of new accessible loading zones.
Establish criteria when on-street accessibility ramps will be installed in conjunction with accessible
loading, adopt design standards for accessible loading zone including ramps and confirm the cost of the
accessibility ramp is the applicant's responsibility. Request for accessible loading zones would be reviewed
and approved through the proposed process, which is very similar to our existing driveway crossing
permit process. The physical construction includes mostly concrete work which is very similar in
nature to the city's driveway crossing program of facilitating driveway crossings and built out
neighborhoods. Accordingly we are recommending alignment of the accessibility ramp application fees
with the fees for driveway crossing permits. These are currently set at $775 per application,
which includes three site inspections by city staff to ensure conformance with standards.
To facilitate all of this, the recommended amendments to city council policy CO7-025-LoadingZones
can be found in appendix three. Thank you for your time. I'm certainly available for any questions.
